newsitem.title: FRANCE: France charges U.S. with dragging feet over Zaire.
newsitem.headline: France charges U.S. with dragging feet over Zaire.

text.p: France criticised the United States on Tuesday for dragging its feet over participation in a multinational force to help end the refugee crisis in eastern Zaire.
"Intervening is urgent and procrastinating by some countries is intolerable," Defence Minister Charles Millon told French radio Europe 1 in an interview.
"The United States must not drag its feet any longer," he said.
France, Spain, Mali and South Africa have pledged troops to an international force to help hundreds of thousands of refugees at risk of dying of hunger and thirst in eastern Zaire.

Canada has offered to lead the force. But the United Nations was still waiting to hear from the United States and Britain, with Washington expected to give its answer on troops for the Central African region before the end of the week.
The U.N. Security Council on Saturday asked members to lay the groundwork for such a force but did not authorise it until its aims and participation were clear.
"It is shocking that the international community is unable to face a humanitarian challenge that will bring about a disaster shortly," he said.
"I hope that we will be able to give an answer in the coming hours. Restoring a small hope to the refugees is urgent," he said.
Paris insists the force of about 5,000 men must be made up of American and African troops as well as European contingents.
Millon said 1,000 French soldiers despatched from France or bases in Africa could be in eastern Zaire within 48 hours if the United Nations reach an agreement on the multinational force.
Millon said military commands in unspecified countries were already making plans to share out operational tasks for their troops in the region.
